venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU
dek: Florida handed it to Baugh until FAU’s linebackers chased him. White left the short throw open, and Florida did not tackle enough of it.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — film session from full SEC broadcast. Fan rail empty until Charles approves.
headline: Florida controlled Saturday because Jadan Baugh made FAU’s linebackers chase the run, and Aaron Philo threw the ball into the grass those linebackers just left. Faulkner’s idea was one run with a changing lead blocker. White’s idea was two safeties deep. The leak was the short throw — 90 plays.

offense.body:
Faulkner’s stressor was simple: make FAU wrong about where Baugh is going, without changing how the play starts.

Aaron Philo lined up in the shotgun — five yards behind the center — and handed the ball to Baugh. All five offensive linemen stepped in one direction. Two of them drove the same FAU tackle, then one of those two left that block and went upfield to pick up a linebacker. Baugh found the hole and hit it. That is the play Florida came back to on first down. The first run after DJ Coleman’s interception was that play: Baugh, up the middle, nine yards from the 6.

FAU had three ways to answer that picture. Faulkner had an answer for each one. If FAU played it straight, Baugh hit the hole. He finished 14 carries, 160 yards, three rushing scores. If FAU sat downhill and waited for that same hole on third-and-2, Faulkner changed who led Baugh. Third quarter, Florida’s own 33, needing two yards. The tight end on the left blocked FAU’s defensive end and held him inside. The left tackle ran around that block and became Baugh’s lead blocker on the edge. Baugh followed the tackle, broke an arm tackle, and ran 61 yards to the 6. He scored from there on the next run. If FAU put extra men on Baugh, or the linebackers stepped up to stop him, Philo threw the leftover grass. He faked the handoff and the tight end was sitting in the space those linebackers just left. Or he threw it immediately and let the tackles and guards get out in front — Bailey Stockton walked it in from the 12. After FAU scored to make it 17–7, Philo threw it over the top to TJ Abrams. Abrams caught it and ran to the 8, 63 yards.

The picture changed before the snap without changing the play. Faulkner sent a receiver walking from one side of the field to the other. If an FAU defender ran with him, Florida knew FAU was in man — each defender has a man. If the defender stayed put, Florida knew FAU was in zone — each defender has an area. Same start. Different answer.

Baugh got the space because the idea is built for him. He moved the chains on first down. Philo moved them when FAU’s corners lined up eight yards off the receiver — Dallas Wilson for 19 on the opening touchdown drive, then the short stop-route and the throw to the sideline. The explosives came from the same idea. Vernell Brown III’s 49-yard touchdown started as a short throw to the right. The first FAU defender missed. Brown was already running. Abrams was the shot over the top when FAU finally crowded the box. Baugh’s 61 was the edge when they sat downhill.

Philo ran the operation. When he got the ball out on time, the idea worked. When he held it, the play died. The interception was Micah Mays Jr. The ball came off his hands. FAU’s Jayden Sweeney was sitting there.

The offensive line was clean — almost no penalties, no late-shift disaster. Assignment sound on the run that won the night. The mistake that loses a real game was not a missed block. Jake Moore snapped the ball over Philo’s head inside the 5. Florida lost twenty yards on that snap.
bullets: Play it straight and Baugh hits the hole — 14 carries, 160 yards, three rushing scores.
Sit downhill on third-and-2 and Faulkner changes who leads: tight end holds the end inside, left tackle leads Baugh 61 yards to the 6.
Crowd Baugh and Philo throws the leftover — Stockton from the 12, Abrams 63, Brown’s 49 after a short throw the first man missed.

defense.body:
White’s lever was the top of the defense. Four linemen on the ball. An extra defensive back to match FAU’s third receiver. Two safeties standing 12 to 15 yards deep. Corners starting 7 to 8 yards off. Rush four. Take away the throw over the top. Live with the five-to-eight yard throw if you tackle it.

The disguise was the linebackers. White walked both of them up into the gaps in front of the center so it looked like six men were coming. At the snap they dropped. Caden Veltkamp would throw the middle, and a linebacker was already standing there.

The throw that stayed open was the short one. FAU never huddled. Veltkamp lived on Dom Henry and Kelby Valsin at five to eight yards. That is how Florida’s defense ran 90 plays. Jon Sumrall said it after the game: on third-and-1, your corner cannot be nine yards off the receiver. That happened.

The job that failed was tackling the catch, and the edge when Veltkamp kept it. Florida stuffed the inside run at the 1 more than once. They still lost the yard. Ethan Ervin scored from a yard out. When the defender on the outside left his spot, Veltkamp ran around him and scored from the 7.

The jobs that succeeded were the ones where Florida’s defensive backs trusted what they saw. Aaron Chiles and DJ Coleman jumped FAU’s throw-it-now screens and blew them up. On the opening drive, third-and-10, Coleman sold the middle of the field. Veltkamp thought the outside receiver was one-on-one. Coleman broke back to the sideline, got over the top of the throw, and intercepted it at Florida’s 5. Later he got a hand on another ball. Dijon Johnson caught that one. The four-man rush got home.

The structure killed the shot over the top. It allowed volume. Ninety plays. A 20-yard touchdown to Valsin in the third quarter.

The fix is people standing where that short throw lands, and they have to tackle it. Keep the edge when the quarterback runs.
bullets: Two safeties deep took away the shot over the top. The short throw stayed open. FAU lived there. Ninety plays.
White walked the linebackers up so it looked like a blitz, then they dropped.
Coleman sold the middle, then intercepted the outside throw at Florida’s 5. The fix is stand on the hitch and tackle it.

specials.body: Patrick Durkin made a 53-yard field goal. That is three points Florida stole from a drive that stalled. Florida never punted. FAU’s 18-yard punt set up Stockton’s touchdown. Specials flipped the field once and added three. They did not give points away.
bullets: FAU’s 18-yard punt set up Stockton’s touchdown.

keys: Offense: hand it to Baugh, change who leads him, throw the leftover.
Defense: two safeties deep, rush four, live with the short throw.
Leak: the short throw. Ninety plays.
Fix: stand on it and tackle it. Do not give a corner nine yards on third-and-1.
Campbell throws it short and Sixkiller runs. That is the leak. Woods stays outside on the keep.

nextWeek.look: Campbell will throw the short ball and their quarterback, Sixkiller, will run. That matches the leak. Florida will still hand it to Baugh. Jayden Woods has to stay on the outside when Sixkiller keeps it.
